subject: Ownership attribution flow & customer data guardrails - Order Form redlines

From: Anna Park <anna.park@clearwell.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@clearwell.com
Subject: Re: Ownership attribution flow & customer data guardrails - Order Form redlines

Thanks for the draft — see attached marked copy with our legal team’s primary concerns. High-level:
- We can’t assign output ownership to Redwood for customer-derived prompts; we need explicit carve-outs.
- Any training/retraining clause must be opt-in and limited to aggregated, de-identified telemetry.
- Feedback license: we can provide feedback to improve service but not grant a perpetual commercial training license without compensation.

I’ve highlighted suggested language in the attached "Clearwell_OrderForm_v2.docx" and added comments in the redline tracker. Can your legal ops propose compromise text for: (1) output title, (2) narrow training consent, (3) internal attribution requirements for model outputs?

Anna
Anna Park | VP Legal, Clearwell Health
anna.park@clearwell.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: Clearwell_OrderForm_v2.docx, redline_tracker.xlsx

Date: 2026-10-05T11:04:00-07:00
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Anna Park <anna.park@clearwell.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, contracts@clearwell.com
Subject: Re: Ownership attribution flow & customer data guardrails - Order Form redlines

Anna — thanks for the thorough pass. Short response while we pull legal language together:

- Output ownership: Redwood’s standard position is customers retain title to outputs they create with the service. The sticking point we see in your redline is the attribution clause that would force customers to display "Powered by Redwood" on all outputs; we can accept a more limited attribution requirement (e.g., internal product notices or marketing references) rather than per-output labeling.
- Training consent: we can offer an opt-in training program with explicit scope: aggregated telemetry only, no PII, and a 90‑day opt-out window. We'd also allow customers to supply allowed data sets for retraining under a separate SOW with compensation.
- Feedback license: propose a time‑bound, non-exclusive license limited to service improvement and safety unless a separate commercial license is negotiated.

I'll loop Marcus (product policy) and Ben (commercial counsel) to draft concrete contract language. If you can flag in the tracker which clauses are dealbreakers vs. negotiable that helps us prioritize.

--
Olga Petrov
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com

Forwarded attachments: Clearwell_OrderForm_v2.docx (annotated), redline_tracker.xlsx

On Thu, Oct 05, 2026 at 11:04 AM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Olga — thanks for the thorough pass. Short response while we pull legal language together:

Adding product context and suggested language below (draft snippets — legal please refine):

1) Output title
- Suggested: "Customer retains ownership of Outputs solely to the extent such Outputs are generated by Customer inputs using the Service. Redwood may not assert ownership over customer-generated Outputs."
- Add carve-out for Redwood’s internal logs/derivatives used solely for diagnostics — not customer-facing assets.

2) Training consent (opt-in)
- Suggested clause: "Customer may opt into Program X for model improvements. Data used will be aggregated and de-identified. Redwood will not use data containing PII or Customer Confidential Information for model training without explicit written agreement and compensation terms."

3) Feedback license
- Suggested: "Customer grants Redwood a limited, revocable license to use Customer Feedback for service improvement for a period of 24 months. For commercial training or model retraining beyond service improvement, a separate license and compensation apply."

I ran this past Product and Security chairs; they flagged telemetry definitions (what counts as PII, what is aggregated) and the enforcement for opt-out timing. Laura — can you prepare a one‑pager describing what telemetry we collect and how we de-identify it so Legal can reference it?

Marcus
Director, Product Policy

2) Telemetry one-pager: Laura — can you attach the one-pager and include the exact sample keys we consider PII vs telemetry? Clearwell wanted concrete examples.
3) Commercial options: propose two paths in the order form: (A) default: "No training consent" with limited feedback license for safety; (B) optional Paid Opt‑In: "Training Package" for customers that want model improvements and grant a time-limited training license (details + SOW + price list).

Anna — we can have a redline back to you by EOD Monday (Oct 12). Would you prefer a short call (20m) to walk the redline or do you want us to send the tracked doc and collect comments asynchronously?
